lemonde.description: Aux yeux des médias comme de l’opposition, l’Etat hébreu fait face à des jours décisifs, bien au-delà du destin personnel de Benyamin Nétanyahou ou de celui des relations avec l’allié historique américain.

Le traumatisme de l’indépendance demeure ancré en Algérie et même chez la diaspora française, du côté des combattants indépendantistes comme des appelés. Ils s'inquiètent aussi de la politique de l'administration américaine qui supprime des outils de surveillance des océans tant dans l'Atlantique que dans le Pacifique.

france24fr.title: Zverev à Roland-Garros : le sacre qui met les médias face à leurs contradictions
france24fr.description: Peut-on célébrer un athlète sans passer sous silence les accusations de violences conjugales qui le visent ? Après la victoire d'Alexander Zverev à Roland-Garros dimanche, les médias français ont choisi de rappeler ce contexte judiciaire. Un traitement qui témoigne d'une évolution du regard porté sur les violences sexistes et sexuelles dans le sport, même si les réflexes d'euphémisation demeurent.

france24fr.title: Mort de Lyhanna : un scandale d'État ?
france24fr.description: "Quand on a un schéma de répétition de faits divers, on est dans un phénomène de société", alerte Laurent Boyet, président et fondateur de l'association "Les Papillons". Ce lundi, des rassemblements sont prévus dans toute la France après le meurtre de Lyhanna, 11 ans, dans le Gers. Les ministres de la justice et de l'intérieur Gérald Darmanin et Laurent Nuñez sont auditionnés pour s'expliquer sur les failles identifiées dans cette affaire.

france24fr.title: Philippines : au moins 15 morts dans un sésime de magnitude 7,8
france24fr.description: Un séisme de magnitude 7,8 a frappé les Philippines, provoquant des secousses violentes ressenties dans plusieurs régions du pays et déclenchant des alertes aux risques de dégâts importants et de possibles répliques. Les autorités parlent d'au moins 15 morts et des dizaines de blessés.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le meilleur arbitre africain 2025 refusé sur le territoire américain
france24fr.description: L'arbitre somalien Omar Abdulkadir Artan, qui devait officier durant la Coupe du monde de football, a été refoulé à son arrivée aux États-Unis, a dénoncé lundi auprès de l'AFP un responsable somalien.

france24fr.title: En Corée du Nord, Xi Jinping promet son "soutien indéfectible" à Kim Jong-un
france24fr.description: En visite de deux jours en Corée du Nord, le président chinois Xi Jinping a dit lundi apporter "son soutien indéfectible" au leader nord-coréen Kim Jong-un, avec qui il éprouve un "sentiment particulier de proximité". Les deux pays se sont engagés à renforcer leurs liens stratégiques et économiques.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : l’incroyable bus scolaire choisi par l’équipe de Curaçao
france24fr.description:
Pour son ultime match avant de s’envoler aux États-Unis, le plus petit pays de la compétition s’est déplacé dans un ancien bus scolaire américain.
 
La nation caribéenne abordera le tournoi dans un groupe E relevé comprenant l’Allemagne, la Côte d’Ivoire et l’Équateur pour la première Coupe du monde de son histoire.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : quelle stratégie de Sonko vis-à-vis de Diomaye Faye ?
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal, Ousmane Sonko a été réélu samedi à la tête du Pastef lors du premier congrès du parti. Cette réélection intervient dans un contexte de rupture avec le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye, qui l’a limogé de la Primature en mai dernier après plusieurs mois de tensions. Fait notable, ni le chef de l’État ni les membres du Pastef restés au gouvernement n’ont été sanctionnés ou exclus du parti. Une stratégie qui interroge alors que le Sénégal traverse une importante recomposition politique. A

france24fr.title: Affaire Lyhanna : "dysfonctionnements" ou manque de moyens de la justice en France ?
france24fr.description: Depuis la découverte du corps de Lyhanna et les révélations sur les plaintes restées lettres mortes visant le principal suspect, le ministre de la Justice Gérald Darmanin a évoqué des "dysfonctionnements" et le non-respect des circulaires pour expliquer le drame. Associations et syndicats de magistrats y voient une manière pour le garde des Sceaux d'évacuer la question récurrente des moyens alloués à la justice.

france24fr.title: En Ukraine, des drones dopés à l'IA
france24fr.description: La cellule des Observateurs de France 24 a analysé des vidéos de l'armée ukrainienne qui montrent des drones en action. Certains modèles utiliseraient l'intelligence artificielle pour se déplacer et repérer sa cible, ce qui pose des questions d'utilisation de l'IA en temps de guerre mais aussi du développement de ces IA. De quoi, pourquoi pas, rebattre les cartes du conflit, comme l'explique le journaliste des Obs Guillaume Maurice.

france24fr.title: RD Congo: Hadja Labib commissaire de l'UE à la coopération internationale en visite à Bunia
france24fr.description: En RD Congo, direction Bunia en Ituri… La province reste l’épicentre de l’épidémie d’Ebola. 86 personnes y sont décédées… 488 cas confirmés y ont été recensé. Ces chiffres sont provisoires car tout le monde ne peut pas encore être testé, les autorités congolaises ne communiquent plus les cas suspects. C’est dans ce contexte que la commissaire de l’Union européenne, Hadja Labib a effectué une visite de terrain.

france24fr.title: Israël et l'Iran cessent leurs attaques après un premier échange de feu depuis avril
france24fr.description: ⁠L'armée iranienne a annoncé lundi que sa première vague d'attaques contre Israël depuis le cessez-le-feu d'avril était désormais terminée, tout en menaçant de reprendre les frappes si Israël poursuivait ses attaques contre le Liban.

france24fr.title: Escalade Iran-Israël : le Liban au cœur des tensions
france24fr.description: Au Moyen-Orient, l’Iran et Israël ont échangé dans la nuit leurs premières frappes directes depuis la trêve conclue il y a deux mois, avant que les deux pays n’annoncent vouloir cesser les attaques. Pour Jean-Loup Samaan, expert associé à l’Institut Montaigne, ces échanges sont surtout un rappel mutuel de leurs capacités de frappe, alors que l’affaiblissement du Hezbollah au Liban reste un enjeu vital pour Téhéran. Donald Trump aurait également fait pression sur Israël pour éviter une nouvelle e

france24fr.title: France : Patrick Bruel placé en garde à vue après des plaintes pour viols et agressions sexuelles
france24fr.description: Patrick Bruel, accusé de viols et d'agressions sexuelles par plusieurs femmes et qui a récemment annulé sa tournée de concerts, a été placé en garde à vue lundi matin, tandis que deux nouvelles plaintes pour viols ont récemment été déposées contre lui.

france24fr.title: Arménie : large victoire du Premier ministre Nikol Pachinian aux législatives
france24fr.description: Le parti du Premier ministre arménien Nikol Pachinian a largement remporté les élections législatives, consolidant son projet de rapprochement avec l’Union européenne et les États-Unis. Cette victoire, saluée par Emmanuel Macron et Ursula von der Leyen, intervient malgré les tensions croissantes avec la Russie, opposée au virage pro-occidental d’Erevan.

france24fr.title: Arménie : Pachinian conforté malgré les tensions avec la Russie
france24fr.description: Selon des résultats partiels, le parti du Premier ministre sortant Nikol Pachinian arrive largement en tête des élections législatives avec plus de 51 % des voix, loin devant l’alliance pro-russe Arménie forte. Ce scrutin, marqué par un taux de participation de 59 %, faisait figure de test pour le dirigeant arménien, engagé depuis plusieurs années dans un rapprochement avec l’Union européenne et les États-Unis au détriment de Moscou.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient : l'inéluctable rupture entre Trump et Netanyahu ?
france24fr.description: Les tensions sont de nouveau montées ces dernières heures au Moyen-Orient après des échanges de frappes entre l’Iran et Israël, les premiers depuis la trêve conclue il y a deux mois. Donald Trump a appelé les deux camps à cesser immédiatement les attaques, un nouvel épisode qui illustre les désaccords croissants entre le président américain et Benjamin Netanyahu sur la gestion du conflit. Analyse avec le chroniqueur Antoine Mariotti, et le correspondant à Washington Matthieu Mabin.

nzz.description: Das Regime versucht, angebliche Differenzen zwischen Trump und Netanyahu auszunutzen und damit Konzessionen am Verhandlungstisch zu erzwingen. Washington sollte hart bleiben.

nzz.title: Der Papst im spanischen Parlament: Ein Appell an Gemeinsamkeit und Humanismus
nzz.description: Leo XIV. hält in Madrid eine historische Rede und wird allseits stürmisch gefeiert. Dabei hatte er nicht nur Komplimente mitgebracht – wie vor allem die Rechtspopulisten erfahren mussten.

nzz.title: Doch keine Millionen für Choupette: Lagerfelds berühmte Katze erhält nichts aus dem Nachlass
nzz.description: Die Katze Choupette war die grosse Liebe des Modeschöpfers Karl Lagerfeld.  Nach seinem Tod hielt sich jahrelang die Legende, das berühmte Haustier werde zur Millionenerbin. Nun hat ein Gericht entschieden: Choupette geht leer aus.

nzz.description: Bei seinem letzten Besuch hatten die Schweizer Behörden den palästinensischen Aktivisten verhaftet und ausgewiesen – zu Unrecht, wie später zwei Gerichte befanden.

observador.description: Artista vencedor de Grammy foi encontrado num jardim na zona de Silvertown. Polícia confirmou a detenção de três pessoas por suspeita de homicídio. Várias celebridades prestaram homenagens.

observador.description: O presidente do Chega atira uma decisão sobre a reforma laboral para depois do encontro. Ainda, o PSD acusa o Chega de apresentar propostas que põem em causa a sustentabilidade da segurança social.

observador.description: Concursos de 2.ª época para colocação de médicos hospitalares foram lançados em dezembro, mas Direção Executiva do SNS não divulga resultados. Sindicatos criticam “opacidade” e pedem "transparência".

observador.description: Carla Barros (PSD) alerta que as medidas do Chega ameaça a sustentabilidade financeira da Segurança Social. Eduardo Teixeira (Chega) diz que as contas estão feitas e que a segurança social pouparia.

observador.description: O regresso do português no fim de semana está, contudo, dependente da aprovação dos médicos do campeonato. O piloto, de 31 anos, sofreu, no início de maio, uma fratura na omoplata.

new-sci.title: You don't need to worry about recursive-self-improving AI – yet
new-sci.description: Anthropic has warned that recursive-self-improving AI could be on the horizon, but the truth is the company is more immediately concerned with marketing itself for a blockbuster initial public offering on the stock market, says Matthew Sparkes

new-sci.title: What really happened when ancient humans migrated out of Africa
new-sci.description: The out-of-Africa migration, in which ancient humans went on to inhabit every other continent except Antarctica, may not have been one moment in time, but a long and slow process. Columnist Michael Marshall examines how archaeologists are rethinking this critical part of our history

new-sci.title: What is a ‘normal’ memory slowdown, and when should I worry?
new-sci.description: Lapses in memory are a normal part of ageing but can also be signs of dementia. Here’s how to distinguish between typical brain ageing and cognitive decline

new-sci.title: Wildlife thrives in solar farm built on restored peatland
new-sci.description: A diverse range of bird species has been recorded at a solar park on rewetted peatland in Germany, suggesting that combining energy generation with habitat restoration could benefit biodiversity, the climate and the economy

new-sci.title: Can Apple and Google stop children from sharing explicit images?
new-sci.description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer has warned tech firms, including Apple and Google, that they must voluntarily implement tools to stop children sharing explicit images, but experts warn this is easier said than done

new-sci.title: Half the world's reservoirs could be clogged up with dirt by 2060
new-sci.description: Each decade the world is losing over 7 per cent of its freshwater storage capacity to sediment build-up, according to an analysis of over half a million reservoirs

new-sci.title: Understanding anorexia’s grip on the brain could unlock new therapies
new-sci.description: One-third of people with anorexia nervosa don’t recover and treatment has remained stagnant for years. Now we’re beginning to understand how the condition takes over the mind

new-sci.title: Unpicking endometriosis reveals how it affects more than the pelvis
new-sci.description: Endometriosis is usually thought of as a gynaecological condition, but a huge study shows it has links with cholesterol levels, inflammation and an altered microbiome

new-sci.title: You could get some of the benefits of sleep without having to nod off
new-sci.description: Mice seemed to reap some of the benefits of sleep by having their brain activity stimulated while they were awake, and the researchers plan to test the approach on people

new-sci.title: Are we getting to the point where it's safe to gene-edit babies?
new-sci.description: A team in the US has reported promising results after using an improved form of CRISPR to gene-edit human embryos, but a major issue remains unsolved

new-sci.title: The maths meme that has been distracting mathematicians for a century
new-sci.description: A seemingly simple set of rules kicks off a kind of mathematical magic trick, which has kept great minds busy since the 1930s. Columnist Jacob Aron explores the origins of the Collatz conjecture, why it is so addictive to mathematicians and whether AI could help us solve it once and for all

new-sci.title: Superintelligent machines may well need us after all
new-sci.description: Despite AI's dizzying improvements in mathematical ability, its successes show just how integral human mathematicians are to the scientific process

new-sci.title: Escher: The paradoxical artist beloved by mathematicians
new-sci.description: A new retrospective of M.C. Escher’s work opens this week. Explore some of his most mind-bending, mathematically inspired works here

new-sci.title: Cuts to US ocean programme will hinder monitoring of El Niño and AMOC
new-sci.description: Scientists warn that the Trump administration's push to dismantle a vital network of ocean-sensing instruments will stymie crucial weather and climate monitoring in the Pacific and Atlantic

new-sci.title: A chromosome from a frozen rat has been resurrected inside mice
new-sci.description: Mice that contain cells with an added rat chromosome have been created by scientists. The next step is to try this with frozen elephant tissue – and if that works, the team will try it with frozen mammoths

new-sci.title: Alice Roberts: 'We are fundamentally, at the end of the day, animals'
new-sci.description: Why do we have big brains? Or walk on two legs? Biological anthropologist and broadcaster Alice Roberts talks human exceptionalism, evolution and her new book Humans with Michael Marshall

new-sci.title: Mysterious ‘cold blob’ in the Atlantic suggests the AMOC is weakening
new-sci.description: A patch of ocean south-east of Greenland is the only place on Earth that is cooling, and it could be a sign that the warm water "conveyor belt" in the Atlantic is slowing down

new-sci.title: Why you need to future-proof your brain in middle age and how to start
new-sci.description: Ages 40 to 65 see a period of turmoil in the brain that has previously been overlooked. But identifying problems during this time can protect your cognitive health for decades to come

phys-org.title: Ribosome tunnel interactions reveal how bacteria can pause protein production
phys-org.description: How do bacteria regulate the production of their proteins? Researchers at the University of Hamburg, in collaboration with international partners, have now demonstrated how small protein building blocks, known as peptides, specifically influence bacterial protein production. The findings have been published in two articles in the journal Nature Communications.

phys-org.title: Need for early, institution-wide AI literacy education highlighted in study
phys-org.description: Along with researchers from James Madison University, three collaborators in the Office of the Provost recently published in Research & Practice in Assessment. Jaime Miller, Stuart Miller and Rachel Whitman Rotch began gathering data in the summer of 2025, investigating students' artificial intelligence (AI) literacy levels using the Generative AI Literacy Assessment Test (GLAT).

phys-org.title: Van der Waals forces can play unexpected role in thin film properties
phys-org.description: Researchers have demonstrated the ability to use van der Waals forces to tune the physical and electronic properties of ferroelectric thin films. The work opens the door to new techniques for engineering materials for use in smaller, more energy efficient electronic devices.

phys-org.title: UN warns of 'deepening crisis' in oceans, urges action
phys-org.description: Oceans are in a "deepening crisis" that demands urgent global action, a major U.N. report warned Monday, with seas warming and rising faster, ice cover shrinking, and marine ecosystems under mounting strain.

phys-org.title: How did a major mangrove restoration project in Senegal end up selling 'ghost carbon?'
phys-org.description: Nature-based solutions have become central to global climate strategies. From tropical forests to wetlands, restoring nature means trees and plants can capture carbon dioxide, reduce global warming, and regenerate biodiversity.

phys-org.title: Neutron star merger simulations gain new precision with AI-driven r-process heating
phys-org.description: Using a novel simulation model based on machine learning, an international research team at GSI/FAIR has succeeded in gaining a deeper understanding of element formation in stellar events such as neutron star mergers. For the first time, the scientists used deep learning with a neural network to model the energy release during r-process nucleosynthesis in hydrodynamic simulations. The results are published in the journal Physical Review D.

phys-org.title: Research uncovers novel electronic properties in quantum material
phys-org.description: Florida State University physicists are part of a team that has discovered unusual superconducting states in parts of graphene, with the potential to drive unexpected quantum technologies.

phys-org.title: Physicists create new family of Schrödinger-cat states
phys-org.description: Quantum mechanics, unlike classical physics, allows objects to exist in more than one state at the same time. This idea is often illustrated by Schrödinger's cat, imagined as being both alive and dead until it is observed. In the laboratory, physicists can create less dramatic but very real versions of this effect by placing atoms, light or motion into two distinct quantum states at once. Creating and controlling these superpositions is essential for applications ranging from quantum comput

phys-org.title: Why sophrosyne, an ancient Greek virtue, matters more than ever in the age of AI
phys-org.description: Texting while driving. Bullying people on social media. Buying into the latest conspiracy theory. Passing off AI-generated work as your own.

phys-org.title: Recovered wild maize gene boosts crop protein without yield loss
phys-org.description: Maize (Zea mays L.) plays an important role in global food security. During 9,000 years of maize domestication and breeding, however, protein content was not a major breeding target. Consequently, many beneficial gene variants associated with higher protein content were gradually lost from cultivated maize. As a result, modern maize varieties often have low seed protein content, leading to a heavy reliance on imported soybean meal for livestock feed.

phys-org.title: What happens when the world's breadbaskets start failing simultaneously?
phys-org.description: Agriculture today is a massive, globally interconnected industry. That interconnectivity has brought jobs and varied foods to people who might not otherwise be able to access them.

phys-org.title: Tabletop experiment helps reconcile fundamental physics
phys-org.description: Assistant Professor Haocun Yu is something of a scientific diplomat. In a recent Physical Review Letters publication, she and her colleagues show how a tabletop experiment can bring together two bedrock physics theories that have never been fully reconciled.

phys-org.title: How Facebook users affected by data breaches react over time examined
phys-org.description: A new study by Mannheim Business Administration professor Hartmut Höhle examines the reactions of actual victims of the Cambridge Analytica scandal on Facebook over a longer period. Its key finding is that, despite being affected by data fraud, users remain on the platform.

phys-org.title: Headless skeletons offer new insights into farming societies 7,000 years ago
phys-org.description: Dozens of human skeletons, lying apparently randomly on and next to each other, with their skulls missing, present a terrifying sight at first glance. Since 2022, this is what researchers have been excavating in a 7,000-year-old settlement near the present-day town of Vráble in Slovakia. Are the headless skeletons the remains of a Neolithic massacre, representing gruesome evidence of a crisis in ancient society?

phys-org.title: California's tectonic stress has reached record level, earthquake model reveals
phys-org.description: Earthquakes usually occur along fracture zones in Earth's crust, where large tectonic plates slide past one another and become locked. Stress builds up over long periods and is suddenly released in the form of an earthquake. In Southern California, the San Andreas and San Jacinto faults are among the most significant of these zones, accommodating most of the plate motion in the region.

phys-org.title: Two decades of research shows Indonesia's coral reefs are heat tolerant—but only up to a point
phys-org.description: Indonesia is home to the world's largest and most biodiverse coral reef system, spanning more than 32,000 square kilometers across the archipelago. Just like what is happening globally, these reefs are now bearing the brunt of a warming ocean.

phys-org.title: Newfound sound wave scattering rule may lead to less bulky, more effective soundproofing
phys-org.description: Researchers in China recently uncovered a quantum-inspired rule governing how sound is scattered by certain physical properties of a material. Their research, published in Physical Review Letters, may lead to the ability to design materials with optimal, broadband sound blocking.

phys-org.title: Study reveals deception and confusion in bankruptcy filings
phys-org.description: Accounting is usually associated with corporations. "In accounting, we traditionally think more about the firm and less about the household," says Fabian Nagel, an assistant professor of accounting at Stanford Graduate School of Business.

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.06518v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sudoku is a representative constraint satisfaction problem that requires global structural reasoning under strict discrete constraints. The existing works of solving Sudoku mainly focus on two dominant approaches, i.e., traditional heuristic and deep learning solver. However, they suffer from two complementary limitations: learning-based solvers lack hard correctness guarantees, while complete symbolic solvers are still prone to long-tail search.

Models are not static objects: they are snapshots of time-evolving processes shaped by data, objectives, architectures, and optimization dynamics. arxiv-ai.description:

Abstract: Self-evolving agents requires adaptation after deployment, but existing approaches assume a usable learning loop, such as curated skills, successful trajectories, or verifier signals. undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Perilous French Gambit
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s increasingly close relationship with France marks a departure from six decades of foreign policy aimed at reducing French influence in West Africa. An increasingly close relationship with a power that has long sought to undermine Nigerian influence in West Africa will benefit only politically connected business elites.

proj-syn.title: Autocracy Is Fueling Mexico’s Fiscal Deterioration
proj-syn.description: Mexico’s recent ratings downgrades are merely a symptom of a more serious malady: the ruling Morena party’s efforts to consolidate power permanently. To ensure the legal predictability foreign investors require, President Claudia Sheinbaum would need to confront Morena’s ideological legacy and, more importantly, its cartel ties.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Economy Is Bad News for Republicans
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump triumphed in the 2024 election by continually hammering on the Biden administration’s dismal inflation record. If his party gets shellacked in this year’s midterm elections, it will be because he has made Americans even worse off.

proj-syn.title: SpaceX Is the New East India Company
proj-syn.description: Although SpaceX is not about to rule over foreign subjects, as the chartered companies founded in the early modern era did, it, too, is operating beyond the reach of any sovereign. And like its predecessors, it has already accumulated immense powers that governments will struggle to reclaim.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

proj-syn.title: The Pope and the AI Profiteers
proj-syn.description: In his first encyclical, Pope Leo XIV rightly rejects the idea that markets alone can be trusted to shape society’s technological future. Recognizing that AI raises questions that prices and profits cannot answer, the Chicago-born pope has posed a direct challenge to Chicago School economics.

proj-syn.title: AI Must Not Encroach on Human Dignity
proj-syn.description: In a world captivated by technological advances, Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical seeks to shift attention away from the marvels and terrors of AI and toward the magnificence of humanity. The message that the technology lacks a “moral conscience” and is distinct from human cognition is necessary and welcome.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.

proj-syn.title: The Living Ghosts of Violent Radicalism
proj-syn.description: Following World War II, the most militant student movements emerged in the former Axis powers as a way to cope with previous generations' complicity. But while the Red Army Faction and others were haunted by memories of past crimes, today's young people have mostly forgotten, and a growing number think far-right politics are cool.

proj-syn.title: Using AI to Test Policy Language
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have long understood that language affects economic behavior, but until recently, there were few tools capable of systematically analyzing its effects. AI may now help close that gap, enabling officials to anticipate how framing and timing can move markets and shift public opinion.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power. The goal is to foreclose any future that is plural, contestable, and beyond the president’s control.

proj-syn.title: How Measles Came Roaring Back
proj-syn.description: Bangladesh is facing soaring measles cases not because of a single localized failure, but because of years of systemic erosion. Ultimately, maintaining herd immunity against highly contagious viruses requires relentless attention to supply and demand, as well as to the broader social and institutional foundations of public health.

proj-syn.title: Pete Hegseth’s Dangerous Call to Arms in Asia
proj-syn.description: Much like it did in Europe, the Trump administration has called on US allies in the Indo-Pacific to increase military spending to 3.5% of GDP.
